raw_text:
name: python-patterns
description: Python development decision-making: framework selection, async, typing, structure. Teach thinking, not copying.
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep

Python principles for 2025. **Learn to THINK, not memorize patterns.** Teach decisions, not fixed code. ASK user for framework preference when unclear. Choose async vs sync based on CONTEXT. Don't default to same framework every time.

Framework: API/microservices or AI/ML serving → FastAPI (async, Pydantic, uvicorn); full-stack/CMS/admin → Django (batteries included); simple/script/learning → Flask. Ask: API-only or full-stack? Need admin? Team familiar with async? Consider async support (FastAPI native, Django 5.0+, Flask extensions), admin, ORM, learning curve.

Async for I/O-bound work, concurrent connections, real-time; sync for CPU-bound, unfamiliar teams, blocking libraries. I/O-bound → async; CPU-bound → sync + multiprocessing. Avoid mixing async/sync carelessly, sync libraries in async code, or async for CPU work. Libraries: HTTP httpx; Redis aioredis / redis-py async; ORM SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Tortoise.

Use inference for locals and scripts; type-hint public APIs. Examples: `Optional[User]`, `str | dict`, `list[Item]`, `dict[str, int]`, `Callable[[int], str]`. Use Pydantic for API models, JSON schema, FastAPI, clear validation errors.

Structure by feature/layer: routes/, services/, models/, schemas/, dependencies/. Django: async ORM limited; async for external API calls, high-concurrency views, background task triggering. Fat models, thin views; managers for common queries; abstract bases for shared fields; class-based complex CRUD, function-based simple endpoints; DRF viewsets; `select_related()` for FKs, `prefetch_related()` for M2M, `.only()` for specific fields.

FastAPI: `async def` with async drivers/HTTP/concurrency; `def` with sync drivers or CPU work (threadpool automatically). Dependencies for auth/current user, testability, cleanup (`yield`). BackgroundTasks: simple in-process; Celery: distributed/complex; ARQ: async Redis; RQ: simple Redis; Dramatiq: actor-based. Consider persistence, fire-and-forget, duration, retries.

Create custom exceptions, register handlers, return consistent errors; raise domain exceptions in services, transform in handlers. Expose error code, human-readable message, applicable field details—not stack traces. Log without exposing internals.

Test unit (pytest), integration (pytest + httpx/TestClient), E2E (pytest + DB); async via `httpx.AsyncClient`, `pytest.mark.asyncio`; fixtures: db_session, client, authenticated_user, sample_data.

Checklist: ask framework preference; choose for context, not default; decide async/sync; plan typing, structure, errors, background tasks. Choose framework based on context. Ask about async requirements. Use Pydantic for validation. Separate concerns (routes → services → repos). Test critical paths. Don’t copy code—choose what serves your application.
